items.stimulus: Archaeology students at a field school test a small replica of an ancient siege catapult. The height above the ground, in feet, of a clay ball $t$ seconds after it leaves the catapult is modeled by $h(t) = -16t^2 + 64t + 5$.
items.stem: For what value of $t$ does $h(t)$ reach its maximum?

B.why: At $t = 4$ the ball comes back down to its launch height of 5 feet. That time is twice the vertex time. You found where the curve reflects across its axis instead of the axis itself.

C.why: 5 is the constant term, which is the height at $t = 0$ (the y-intercept). It tells you nothing about when the maximum happens.

D.why: 69 feet is the maximum height, $h(2)$. That is the y-value of the vertex, but the question asks for the time $t$ when the maximum happens.
